newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-TIRIAC CALLS FOR DAVIS CUP ONCE EVERY FOUR YEARS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-TIRIAC CALLS FOR DAVIS CUP ONCE EVERY FOUR YEARS.

text.p: Boris Becker's former coach Ion Tiriac said on Sunday the annual Davis Cup team competition should be played once every four years.

"A day should come sooner or later when the Davis Cup is run once every four years, two years after the Olympic Games. It would then really have a world champion of nations," the Romanian tennis official and former player said.
"I would prefer it on one surface. Possibly in a 10-day or two week period.
Tiriac organises major tournaments and Davis Cup ties.

Last week Australian Open champion Becker, Pete Sampras and Andre Agassi called for the Davis Cup to be played less often because of the stress on players. The two Americans suggested it should be played every two years.
On Sunday, Association of Tennis Professionals (ATP) chief Mark Miles said the Davis Cup was becoming a headache.
"It is clear that the Davis Cup is the most difficult aspect of men's professional tennis to schedule," Miles said. "There is unanimity among the players that this is a problem to be addressed."
At present the competition is held over four rounds in February, April, September and November/December.
Neither Sampras nor Agassi played a role in U.S. ties this year. The champions failed to make it to the semifinals after crashing out to the Czech Republic.
World number one Sampras said the Cup was being "degraded" because the top players were not taking part.
